<딛1:5> 내가 너를 그레데에 떨어뜨려 둔 이유는 부족한 일을 바로잡고:
<Titus 1:5> For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting, and ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee:
 - The reason he left Titus behind was to appoint elders. By status or position it's "elder," and by the work it's "bishop," but the Methodist and Presbyterian churches each use them separately. That's odd too.
<딛1:6~9> 책망할 것이 없고 한 아내의 남편이며 방탕하다 하는 비방: <Titus 1:6~9> If any be blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of riot or unruly. For a bishop must be blameless, as the steward of God; not selfwilled, not soon angry, not given to wine, no striker, not given to filthy lucre; but a lover of hospitality, a lover of good men, sober, just, holy, temperate; holding fast the faithful word as he hath been taught, that he may be able by sound doctrine both to exhort and to convince the gainsayers.
<딛2:1~10> 오직 너는 바른 교훈에 합한 것을 말하여 늙은 남자로는: <Titus 2:1~10> But speak thou the things which become sound doctrine: that the aged men be sober, grave, temperate, sound in faith, in charity, in patience.
늙은 여자로는 이와 같이 행실이 거룩하며 참소치 말며 많은 술의 종이 되: The aged women likewise, that they be in behaviour as becometh holiness, not false accusers, not given to much wine, teachers of good things; that they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, to be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed.
너는 이와 같이 젊은 남자들을 권면하여 근신하게 하되 범사에 네 자신으로:
Young men likewise exhort to be sober minded. In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you. Exhort servants to be obedient unto their own masters, and to please them well in all things; not answering again; not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.
 - Through the good works of Christ's people, God's teaching is made to shine.
<딛3:1~11> 허탄한 신화 족보를 버리라. 이단에 빠진 사람은 한두:
<Titus 3:1~11> Throw out empty fables and genealogies. Warn someone caught in heresy once or twice, then keep away from him. And so on
 - Paul's exhortations keep coming
<딛3:12~14> 내가 아데마나 두기고를 네게 보내리니 그 때에 네가:
<Titus 3:12~14> When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis: for I have determined there to winter. Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them. And let ours also learn to maintain good works for necessary uses, that they be not unfruitful.
 - The word "lawyer" appears only once in the New Testament, and it means a person who makes church law.
 - Paul urges them to send people ahead early and learn to devote themselves to the good work of preparing what's needed. If you prepare long and do it thoroughly, even if the ministry period is short, it bears fruit.
<딛3:15>나와 함께 있는 자가 다 네게 문안하니 믿음 안에서 우리를:
<Titus 3:15>All that are with me salute thee. Greet them that love us in the faith. Grace be with you all.
 - Titus was a truly outstanding man; seeing that he resolved the problems of the Corinthian church, and that Paul left him in Crete, where evil and lazy people lived, he was someone who went to hard places and did the work well. On to 2 Timothy~
